<!--

issue_context.title: Custom integration breaking change with PR #124102
issue_context.body:
### The problem

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/124102 adds a correct validation of [`is_entity_service_schema`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/55c42fde88c7a6989a8489b755375fef92360f35/homeassistant/helpers/config_validation.py#L1308). 
However, this is a breaking change for (custom) integrations. 
For example, it broke [this](https://github.com/amitfin/daily_schedule/actions/runs/10625365675/job/29455199692) (which was fixed by [that](https://github.com/amitfin/daily_schedule/pull/92/files#diff-20616c1e7cebd791697f5125e5180e8bf5f220729864d37436726b740eb77817)).
Maybe we should make the change more gradual and allow a migration period?

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.9.0b1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2024.8.3

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

daily_schedule

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://github.com/amitfin/daily_schedule

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
comments: you already reported this earlier with #124913 but closed it without any comments?

The issue was recreated using the link from the beta release notes with the hope that it will be marked as a beta issue. But apparently it doesn't matter.
Hopefully, someone will pick it up as it might become a big issue with the upcoming release.

review_comments: Why don't we raise an error in core if already all services are correct?
Core means "we did not find an integration when unwinding the stack frame", not "called by a core integration", so I'd rather not raise.
